meta.title: Reimagining Checkout for Global Scale
meta.oneLiner: Reduced cart abandonment by 23%, recovering $4.2M in annual revenue

hero.title: Reimagining Checkout for Global Scale
hero.outcome: Reduced cart abandonment by 23%, recovering $4.2M in annual revenue
hero.heroAlt: Streamlined 2-step checkout flow showing payment and confirmation screens

tldr: Acme Commerce's checkout flow was losing $18M annually to abandonment due to a fragmented 5-step process with hidden trust signals. I led a 4-month redesign that consolidated it to 2 steps, added smart defaults for international users, and surfaced trust badges at decision points. The result: 23% higher completion rates and $4.2M in recovered annual revenue.

context.businessProblem: Acme Commerce processes $2B in annual transactions across 40 countries. Despite strong brand recognition, conversion from cart to purchase lagged competitors by 15 percentage points. Checkout abandonment cost the company an estimated $18M annually.
context.background: The existing checkout flow was built 4 years prior for US-only customers. As Acme expanded internationally, the flow accumulated patches without a coherent redesign. Trust signals were buried, address formats confused international users, and forced account creation drove away one-time buyers.

responsibilities: Owned end-to-end checkout UX across web and mobile
Led a team of 2 designers, conducting weekly design critiques
Partnered with Data Science to define success metrics
Facilitated stakeholder alignment across 3 business units
Collaborated daily with engineering on feasibility trade-offs
myRole.collaboration: I worked embedded with the Checkout team (1 PM, 5 engineers, 1 researcher) and coordinated with the International Growth team for localization requirements.
myRole.ownership: I defined the design strategy, success metrics, and prioritization framework. I made final design decisions with input from research and engineering constraints.

constraints: 4-month timeline to ship before holiday shopping peak
Must maintain backward compatibility with 3 legacy payment provider APIs
Localization for 12 languages with no dedicated localization team
No dedicated researcher—I conducted guerrilla testing myself
Mobile web conversion critical (62% of traffic, 40% of revenue)

methods: Session recordings analysis (10,000 sessions via Fullstory)
User interviews (12 participants across US, UK, Germany)
keyFindings: 67% of users abandoned at the payment step—trust signals were hidden below fold on mobile
International users spent 40% longer on address entry due to US-centric field ordering
Guest checkout was buried in a secondary tab, forcing unnecessary account creation
Users hesitated at final confirmation due to unclear total cost breakdown
evidence: Heatmaps showed 80% of mobile users never scrolled to see security badges
Session recordings revealed users abandoning after encountering 'State/Province' before 'Postal Code'
Survey data: 34% of abandoned carts cited 'didn't want to create an account'

quotes.text: I just want to buy this one thing. Why do I need to create an account?
I wasn't sure if the total included shipping until the very end. That's frustrating.

hmw: How might we surface trust signals at key decision points?
How might we adapt the flow for international address expectations?
How might we make guest checkout the obvious path for one-time buyers?

process.description: Analyzed existing data, conducted user research, and aligned stakeholders on the problem definition and success metrics.

decisions.tradeoffs: Mobile-first meant desktop would inherit some touch-optimized patterns, but data showed mobile was the critical conversion gap.
decisions.rationale: 62% of traffic was mobile but conversion was 15pp lower than desktop. Fixing mobile had highest ROI.

process.description: Explored 3 structural approaches and tested quick prototypes with users before committing to a direction.

decisions.tradeoffs: More complex to build (+2 weeks engineering), but accommodated both scanning and stepping behaviors.
decisions.rationale: User testing showed 40% of users prefer to scan all information, 60% prefer to focus on one section. Hybrid served both without forcing a choice.

decisions.tradeoffs: Potential reduction in account creation, but account team agreed conversion was priority.
decisions.rationale: 34% of abandoned carts cited forced account creation. Defaulting to guest removed friction; users who wanted accounts could still opt in.

process.description: Built high-fidelity prototypes, tested with 45 users across 3 markets, and iterated based on feedback.

decisions.decision: Sticky order summary with running total
decisions.tradeoffs: Takes vertical space on mobile, but testing showed users valued constant cost visibility.
decisions.rationale: Users abandoned when unsure of total. Sticky summary with shipping estimate reduced uncertainty at every step.

decisions.decision: Smart address lookup with market-specific field ordering
alternatives: Standard US field order for all
decisions.tradeoffs: Required integration with address validation API and conditional logic, adding 1 week to timeline.
decisions.rationale: International users struggled with US-centric forms. Smart lookup reduced fields from 7 to 2 and ordered remaining fields by market convention.

solution.overview: A streamlined 2-step checkout flow with smart defaults, prominent trust signals, and seamless international support. Guest checkout is default, with one-click account creation at confirmation.

features.name: Trust Badges Above Fold
features.description: Security badges, payment icons, and money-back guarantee moved to fixed position visible on first load.
features.annotation: 67% of users previously abandoned at payment step—trust signals were hidden below fold

features.name: Smart Address Lookup
features.description: Postal code lookup that auto-fills city/state and reorders fields based on user's locale.
features.annotation: Reduced address fields from 7 to 2 for most users; international users see locale-appropriate field order

features.name: Guest Checkout Default
features.description: No account required. Users can optionally save info with one checkbox after purchase.
features.annotation: Addressed the #1 abandonment reason: 'didn't want to create an account'

features.name: Sticky Order Summary
features.description: Running total with shipping estimate visible at all times, updating dynamically as options change.
features.annotation: Users wanted clarity on total cost at every step—eliminated end-of-flow surprises

testing: Moderated usability testing (12 participants) on prototype
Unmoderated testing (45 participants) across US, UK, Germany
A/B test (50,000 users, 2 weeks) for trust badge placement
iterations: Changed 'Apply coupon' link to button after 3/12 users missed it
Reordered address fields by market after international users struggled with US format
Changed 'Express checkout' label to 'Pay with saved info' after confusion in testing
Added estimated delivery date to order summary after user feedback
feedback: A/B test: Trust badges above fold outperformed by 8%—shipped to 100%
Support tickets dropped 18% in first month after launch

qualitative: Featured in company all-hands as Q3 highlight
Checkout approach adopted by 3 other product teams
Design system team incorporated components into shared library
Received 4.8/5 in post-launch user survey (up from 3.9)

learnings: Localization should start day 1, not be retrofitted—we burned 2 weeks fixing field ordering issues that could have been avoided
Stakeholder alignment workshops saved us 3 weeks of rework—the upfront investment paid off
Guerrilla testing is better than no testing—even 5-minute hallway tests caught major issues
whatWouldChange: Involve engineering earlier in ideation—we hit avoidable technical debt on the address API integration
Set up metrics tracking before launch—we had a 2-week data gap while analytics was configured
Document design decisions in real-time—reconstructing rationale for this case study was harder than it should have been

nextSteps: One-click reorder for returning customers (in progress)
Saved payment methods for logged-in users
